$comment: THE ONE REGISTRY for the sheet's knobs (ADR-114) and the arcs instrument's (ADR-118). Read by the pages (TS import, through lib/sheet/directions.ts) and by scripts/capture-subpages.mjs (readFileSync), and mirrored into the ship's armada.toml. Two readers, one record: a direction cannot be shot that the page cannot draw. TYPE IDS ARE LETTERS ONLY - the armada's filename grammar takes letters before the first dash. THE FIRST VALUE OF EVERY KNOB IS THE HOUSE: direction SB is every knob at its first value, and every other direction is an argument someone has to make against it. A direction's `types` scopes it to the pages whose knobs it moves (absent = every page): SD and SE move the document pages' head, ordinals, pile and timeline; SG and SL move the arcs instrument's span and frame, which only /arcs and its fixture kit draw. The `rules` knob (two full-height rules at the band's edges, or seams alone) was DELETED on 2026-09-20 by the owner's ruling - the frame's rails are the page's only verticals - and its seams direction SC went with it (ADR-114 U1). The `rows` knob (ruled one-line rows, or boxed plates) was DELETED on 2026-09-21 with its direction SH (ADR-118 U1): the owner read the ruled log as 'a glorified word document' and asked for blocks, and the house went past both values - one bordered block per engagement, a gutter, no group heads. SA and SF are not knob sets: they are NEGATIVE POLES. SA is the old /arcs, shot once before the sheet replaced it; SF is the sheet's own overview, promoted byte-identical from wave-02-sb before the instrument replaced it (`from`). The `dossier` knob (one housing, or an image plate over a text plate) was DELETED on 2026-09-21 with its direction SJ (ADR-118 U2): the dossier's picture went, replaced by the client's configuration drawn, and a pair of plates had nothing left to split.

head.label: Head
head.note: split = the title in the left five columns and the paragraphs opposite (Hermeus). stack = the kicker alone on the left and the title with its paragraphs stacked on the right. The owner's sentence reads both ways; the wave decides.

ordinal.label: Ordinal
ordinal.note: on = every section's head band letters 01 / 02 / … (Hermeus, Prime Intellect: ordinals as wayfinding). off = the kicker alone (the casefile's own no-ordinal ruling, ADR-066).

card.label: Cards
card.note: stack = the console's flashcards stack on scroll under a sticky panel (the proof stack's mechanic). grid = the same cards in a static two-column grid.

timeline.label: Timeline
timeline.note: axis = a horizontal dated axis with the sessions seated on it at their dates (Hermeus roadmap). rail = a vertical date rail with the sessions opposite (Hermeus detail) — also the phone's own layout.

span.label: Span
span.note: The arcs monitor's time axis. active = whole weeks from the first filed engagement to now; a relationship older than the axis enters open from the left edge. full = the whole record since the oldest relationship, linear — honest, and it buries nine marks in its last twentieth.

frame.label: Frame
frame.note: The arcs monitor's edges. housing = one bounded housing on the instrument band, every rule ending on its own edge. rails = the header and foot strips run out to the HUD's rails, the literal reading of 'we already have our rails' and wave 02's unanswered question.

directions.name: Old arcs
directions.question: the negative pole: what the owner said looks bad, byte-identical, so every check that names it can be shown to fail it
directions.shape: a centred hero over a gutter grid of chamfered posters, no page rules

directions.name: Sheet arcs
directions.question: the second negative pole: the sheet overview the owner asked to replace with an instrument, byte-identical, so every monitor and log check can be shown to fail it
directions.shape: a split head over one console per client and a two-by-two of house formats

directions.name: House
directions.question: does every page read as one grammar at its own values — the document pages as ruled sheets, the arcs overview as one instrument — across both themes and both viewports?
directions.shape: the ruled sheet: split head, ordinals, the pile, the axis; on the arcs overview the monitor and the log

directions.name: Editorial
directions.question: does the head read better stacked on the right with no ordinals, or does the page lose its wayfinding?
directions.shape: kicker left, title and paragraphs stacked right, no section numerals

directions.name: Grid
directions.question: does a static grid of flashcards and a vertical date rail say the same thing as the pile and the axis, with less motion?
directions.shape: cards in two columns, the sessions on a rail

directions.name: Full record
directions.question: does the whole record on one linear axis say more than the active window, or does it bury nine marks in its last twentieth?
directions.shape: the same monitor on an axis from the oldest relationship to now

directions.name: Rails
directions.question: do the monitor's strips read as part of the frame when they run out to the HUD's rails, or does a rule that meets a rail read as a second frame?
directions.shape: the monitor's header and foot strips running to the rails

wave.note: Each direction on its own types x 2 themes at the default viewport, one still per section (the arcs log adds a third still, after a second engagement is picked); laptop for SB first. 1920x1247 is the owner's own window; 1280x720 is the binding one.
